title: Public modular fold evidence workload
objective: Implement an authenticated phase runner and independent oracles for the measured public bounded modular Horner workload, including complete generic, V8 lower-bound, and unavailable target dispositions, without changing the shared workload catalog.

oracles: Independent CPython and JavaScript exact residue

handoff.summary: Implemented the public modular-fold evidence runner and focused tests. The runner measures complete public polynomial_evaluate_mod calls in fresh Sage.js O0 and O2 processes, records an independent non-overlapping validation/normalization and Horner-fold partition, checks exact CPython and independent BigInt JavaScript oracles, and retains explicit unavailable library/native/Wasm outcomes. Its complete handwritten safe-Number implementation is mechanically labeled a non-production lower bound. The workload is explicitly a compiler-control and target-mismatch negative-evidence microbenchmark: the dense-list source contract requires mature fmpz_mod_poly algorithms for production large inputs. Exact profiler-envelope source paths are emitted in receipts. No shared catalog was edited.
risks: This workload is ineligible for dense-list production promotion; large-input production operations must use mature fmpz_mod_poly algorithms.

The normalization and fold samples are disjoint timers from one equivalent partitioned execution, not values subtracted from the complete public-call timer; timer observation overhead can therefore make their sum exceed the independently measured complete call.
The runner disables the unrelated stale hyperelliptic auto-receipt policy only inside its non-hyperelliptic child processes; cross-platform promotion must validate that receipt independently.

The standard changed-file unit sweep is presently blocked by the unrelated stale hyperelliptic receipt, and with that policy disabled test/cache-automatic.cjs did not settle while another campaign was using the shared cache. Focused tests, the full compiler suite, build, merge checks, and architecture checks passed.

Treat the generic O2 result as compiler-control evidence and the Number result as a non-production lower bound; do not infer production eligibility until a complete mature-library route exists.
